The test image shows a split soybean stem with:
- Bleached/straw-colored stem tissue
- Black sclerotia (hard, irregular black bodies) inside the pith
- White cottony mycelium visible
- Longitudinal cracking of the stem

This is highly characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot). Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference confirms it: White Mold shows bleached stem tissue with black sclerotia protruding through the stem surface. The test image matches perfectly — split stem with black sclerotia inside the pith and white mycelium, which is the textbook internal view of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).
